status: Well-defined native editing workflows retain strict document, history and pixel comparisons. Undefined alpha-refit geometry and incorrect short-stroke origin painting use authored correctness invariants instead of historical memory-dependent output. Runtime verification is recorded separately.
rootLimit: Native alpha-premultiplied refitting reloads two live colors while edited regions still identify color slot 2, then reads outside its palette. Historical NaNs and arbitrary coordinates are not a valid output oracle. The independent implementation must complete finite fitted geometry and serialization while retaining painted region colors.
colorOwnership: Edited region color IDs belong to the creation palette, which remains authoritative for contour and output colors. Each smoothing run owns a complete sampling table initialized from those slots, then overlays the entire current live processing palette at the same indices, extending storage if needed. Selected controls therefore retain native sampling semantics for their defined prefix; edit-owned trailing slots survive profile reload without dangling references. The exposed live palette remains the selected processing palette, not the creation palette.
samplingBoundary: Build the complete sampling table before passing geometry to smoothing, independently of anti-aliasing, cancellation or palette length. Anti-aliasing disabled still skips coordinate color sampling. Keep boundary validation: all region color IDs must be nonnegative integers and enabled sampling must find every ID in its owned table. Never clamp IDs, substitute a palette after validation fails, or reproduce undefined memory.
shortStrokePolicy: A subpixel pencil segment crossing a pixel boundary paints both endpoint pixels and no distant origin. Native computes fewer than two samples for these segments and its captured origin pixel is incorrect. Preserve strict native tool, color and dimension checks. Assert authored complete pixels, serialized records and undo/redo transitions for corrected strokes, including no history entry for a later move inside an already-painted pixel. Retain strict native history/key checks for unaffected gestures. Do not edit historical captures.
scope: Advanced guided segmentation edits followed by Back, Start, Reset or Next. Compare live editor pixels, undo/redo records and keys, selected profile, palette runtime and complete document state.
referenceBoundary: A separate opt-in helper submits declared ToolActionRecord values to the original takeAction(ToolActionRecord,bool) model slot. It never sends native mouse/key events or answers native dialogs. Replay's active-modal abort guard remains enabled. Accepted reference executables stay unchanged.
observation: After Edit Segmentation has initialized the owned QImage, read it and the selected profile's undo/redo histories on later model snapshots while a source exists. Before entry or after full reset, read only the constructed history lists. Do not treat absent editor-image observations as cleared pixels.
completion: Repeat native responses byte-for-byte, reparse complete responses, preserve all original installation files/settings/input desktop, then pass differential engine/service tests and real React checks for any necessary implementation changes.
historyScope: 55 native observations compare undo/redo counts. Available image observations additionally compare dimensions, serialized edit keys and every opaque display pixel. Individual binary history payloads are retained, not exposed by the GUI owner for direct comparison.
browserScope: Real green color selection, Fill at pixel 2,2, Next, smoothing timer and Back. Exact native SVG, controls and region/history counts match. Prepared native commands use zero unused Fill coordinates; browser gestures use -1 sentinels. Do not claim serialized stage-key equality across those forms.
